title: Caesar Cipher
description:
Encrypt a message using a Caesar cipher: shift every letter forward by k positions in the alphabet, wrapping around from z to a. Uppercase letters stay uppercase, lowercase stay lowercase. All other characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) are unchanged.

Input

  • Line 1: the message s
  • Line 2: an integer k (0 ≤ k ≤ 1000)

Output

The encrypted message.

title: Palindrome Sentence
description:
Determine whether a sentence is a palindrome when you ignore case and every character that is not a letter or digit.

Input

A single line s.

Output

YES if it is a palindrome, otherwise NO.
solution:
s = input()
t = [c.lower() for c in s if c.isalnum()]
print("YES" if t == t[::-1] else "NO")

tests.input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
Was it a car or a cat I saw?

title: Anagram Check
description:
Two words are anagrams if one can be formed by rearranging the letters of the other. Comparison is case-insensitive.

Input

  • Line 1: word a
  • Line 2: word b

Output

YES if they are anagrams, otherwise NO.
solution:
a = input().lower()
b = input().lower()
print("YES" if sorted(a) == sorted(b) else "NO")

title: Vowels and Consonants
description:
Count the vowels (a e i o u, either case) and the consonants (all other English letters) in a line. Non-letter characters are ignored.

Input

A single line s.

Output

Two lines: Vowels: V and Consonants: C.

title: Reverse Each Word
description:
Reverse the letters of every word in a sentence while keeping the words in their original order. Words are separated by single spaces.

Input

A single line of words separated by single spaces.

Output

The sentence with each word reversed.

title: Capitalize Each Word
description:
Make the first character of each word uppercase and the rest of the word lowercase. Words are separated by single spaces.

Input

A single line of words separated by single spaces.

Output

The sentence with every word capitalized.
solution: print(' '.join(w[:1].upper() + w[1:].lower() for w in input().split(' ')))

title: Run-Length Encoding
description:
Compress a string using run-length encoding: each maximal run of the same character is written as the character followed by the length of the run. For example, aaabb becomes a3b2.

Input

A single non-empty string s of lowercase letters.

Output

The encoded string.
solution:
s = input()
r = []
i = 0
while i < len(s):
    j = i
    while j < len(s) and s[j] == s[i]:
        j += 1
    r.append(s[i] + str(j - i))
    i = j
print(''.join(r))

title: Missing Letters
description:
A pangram is a sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet at least once. Find which letters (case-insensitive) are missing from the given sentence.

Input

A single line s.

Output

The missing letters in lowercase, in alphabetical order, with no spaces. If none are missing, print PANGRAM.
solution:
s = set(input().lower())
m = ''.join(c for c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' if c not in s)
print(m if m else "PANGRAM")

title: Most Frequent Letter
description:
Find the letter that appears most often in the text, ignoring case and non-letter characters. If several letters tie, choose the one that comes first alphabetically. The text contains at least one letter.

Input

A single line s.

Output

The most frequent letter in lowercase followed by a space and its count.

tests.input: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

title: Toggle Case
description:
Change every uppercase letter to lowercase and every lowercase letter to uppercase. Other characters are unchanged.

Input

A single line s.

Output

The toggled string.
solution:
s = input()
print(''.join(c.lower() if c.isupper() else c.upper() for c in s))

title: Count Set Bits
description:
Count the number of 1 bits in the binary representation of a non-negative integer n. Try to use bitwise operators (&, >>).

Input

A single integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 1018).

Output

The number of set bits.
solution:
n = int(input())
c = 0
while n:
    n &= n - 1
    c += 1
print(c)

title: Power of Two
description:
Determine whether a given integer n is a power of two. Hint: a positive power of two has exactly one set bit, so n & (n - 1) is 0.

Input

A single integer n (-109 ≤ n ≤ 1018).

Output

YES if n is a power of two, otherwise NO.
solution:
n = int(input())
print("YES" if n > 0 and n & (n - 1) == 0 else "NO")

title: Decimal to Binary
description:
Convert a non-negative integer n to its binary representation without using bin() or format(). Use & 1 and >> instead.

Input

A single integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 1018).

Output

The binary representation of n with no leading zeros (0 for zero).

title: Find the Single Number
description:
Every number in the list appears exactly twice except for one number that appears once. Find that number. Hint: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, so XOR-ing all numbers leaves only the single one.

Input

  • Line 1: an odd integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105)
  • Line 2: n space-separated integers

Output

The number that appears only once.
solution:
n = int(input())
r = 0
for x in map(int, input().split()):
    r ^= x
print(r)

title: Flip the Bits
description:
Flip every bit of a positive integer n within its own bit-length (no leading zeros), then print the resulting number. For example, 5 is 101; flipping gives 010 = 2. Hint: XOR with a mask of all ones of the same length.

Input

A single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1018).

Output

The integer obtained after flipping the bits.
solution:
n = int(input())
mask = (1 << n.bit_length()) - 1
print(n ^ mask)

title: Hamming Distance
description:
The Hamming distance between two integers is the number of bit positions at which their binary representations differ. Hint: count the set bits of a ^ b.

Input

Two non-negative integers a and b on one line, separated by a space (0 ≤ a, b ≤ 1018).

Output

The Hamming distance between a and b.
solution:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
x = a ^ b
c = 0
while x:
    c += x & 1
    x >>= 1
print(c)
